newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Century Inn eyes more managed pubs.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Century Inn eyes more managed pubs.

text.p: British pub operator Century Inns Plc said on Friday it expected to expand its managed pub business by about 20 houses a year to help pump profits higher.

Century, which agreed to buy 78 managed houses from Pubmaster for about 35.1 million stg, said it was striving to increase its managed pub operations, which were more profitable than its core tenanted pub business.
"I would have thought we'd be putting on maybe another 20 managed houses per annum, something of that sort," chief executive Alistair Arkley told Reuters in an interview.

He added that the company planned to spend at least 10 million stg a year to develop its managed pub business, while spending on tenancies would stay roughly unchanged at 1.0-2.0 million stg per year.
Century Inns currently has about 400 tenanted pubs and 23 managed houses, mostly in northeast England.
Managed pubs tend to have lower-cost profits than tenanted pubs, partly because the houses are managed by company employees rather than tenants.
Arkley said that although managed pubs would now represent only 20 percent of all of its pubs, they would make up about 30 percent of its profits and 50 percent of its turnover on a pro forma basis.
"We're becoming a much more balanced managed and tenanted business than we were historically," he said.
